question: How does the course waitlist work at CSUB?
answer:
When a seat opens, the waitlist process considers each student in order and will not move a student into the course if any of these three are true:
any prerequisites are not met;
adding the waitlist course would put the student at or above their unit limit;
the student would have a time conflict with the course.
If you are enrolled in 12 or more units, you are limited to 15 units of waitlist courses. If enrolled in fewer than 12 units, you may request permission from the Dean of your school to be on more waitlists.
If you are added to a section from the waitlist, you will receive an email. Students on waitlists should check their myCSUB account daily to see if they have been added.
Waitlists are cleared after the Last Day to Add for the semester.

Academic advising is a form of teaching integral to the institution’s teaching and learning mission. Advisors help students value the learning process, apply decision-making strategies, set priorities, develop thinking and learning skills, and make informed choices.
Advising involves helping students plan their academic path, understand degree requirements, stay on track from first semester through graduation, and connect with campus resources.
CSUB uses a case management model: each undergraduate is assigned a Staff Advisor in an advising center who is the primary contact and helps students stay on track with degree requirements, connect with resources, and navigate challenges. CSUB materials recommend developing a coordinated advising program (including vision, mission, student learning outcomes, advising curriculum, onboarding/professional development for advisors, and a Proactive Caseload Management Advising Program) and forming an Advising Council to guide and monitor those efforts.

question: What health services are available to CSUB students?

question: How do I apply to live in on-campus student housing?
answer:
To apply for on-campus student housing at CSU Bakersfield:

Submit your Intent to Enroll

Log into myCSUB and follow the steps in your To-Do list to submit your Intent to Enroll by the posted deadline (example: November 14, 2025 for certain cohorts).

Apply for Housing

1–2 business days after accepting your offer of admission (once the housing application is open), go to your CSUB Housing Portal to secure housing.
Complete your housing profile: create a bio visible to roommates/suitemates, confirm contact and emergency contact info, select top room-type preferences (prices vary and preferences are not guaranteed), and sign your housing license agreement (a 9-month academic-year contract).
You will receive a confirmation email when your housing application is complete. Room assignments and room-type confirmations are based on the date you completed your housing profile and signed your license agreement.

Pay required housing advance payment

Complete the University Residence Hall contract online with your housing advance payment (or apply with a Private Certified Housing facility if applicable).

Complete required new-student steps

Submit official transcripts, register for orientation, set up an academic advising appointment, apply for financial aid, and check your myCSUB To-Do List for any additional requirements.

Notes:

First-year housing requirement: entering first-time freshmen enrolled in 12 or more units for Fall and residing more than 60 miles from CSUB are required to live on campus for their first academic year unless exempted (special exemptions considered case-by-case).
Residence hall occupancy and room configurations are subject to change.
For more information, visit the CSUB Student Housing & Residence Life webpage.
